reason: The trigger is real but outside the window: the $650M Series C led by TWG Global closed on 13 April 2026 (TechCrunch; WardsAuto; ~$1.4B raised to date), which is 145 days before the row's date against a 90-day limit. Nothing newer qualifies as a capital or identity inflection: reservations opened on 30 June 2026 (InkFreeNews, reported), a factory tour was given on 28 August 2026 (fwbusiness.com, reported) and first deliveries are guided to the fourth quarter of 2026 (WardsAuto) — the start of production is the next real trigger and has not happened. The row is also wrong on the decision-maker: Peter Faricy (ex-Amazon Marketplace, ex-SunPower CEO) has been CEO since March 2026 and runs commercial, digital, finance and legal; founding CEO Chris Barman is President of Vehicles (TechCrunch 9 Mar 2026, electrive 11 Mar 2026). Not contradicted, not an existing F1/FE partner. Worth holding: TWG Global, which led the Series C, owns TWG Motorsports, the parent of Andretti Formula E and co-owner of the Cadillac F1 Team, so the warm path the row noted on the F1 side applies equally to Andretti in FE. Re-open at start of production / first deliveries (Q4 2026) with Faricy as the decision-maker and the Austin (6 Feb 2027) and Miami (20 Feb 2027) E-Prix as the launch window; the $24,950 truck is a consumer-EV story the all-electric series can carry.
